title: Jarvis — Personal Voice Assistant
tagline: Local voice assistant with a visual Second Brain and two AI engines

simple.tagline: A personal assistant I talk to, and it answers — running on my own computer.
simple.summary: I wanted an assistant that brought together my calendar, email and news in one place, without paying a subscription and without sending my personal life outside my computer. So I built one: I talk, it answers. It reads my calendar, sorts my emails into three priority buckets, and gives me a spoken summary of my day each morning. It also organizes my notes — 22 of them, across 7 areas — and sends them to my digital notebook with one click.

problem: I wanted a personal voice assistant that centralized my agenda, email and news without depending on any paid service and without duplicating logic I had already built in other personal projects.
targetUser: Personal use (agenda and personal life / university handball; same scope as agenda-pessoal, no work-related data whatsoever).
myRole: Sole developer: architecture, frontend, local server and integration with both AI engines.
process: Built in three incremental parts, always enveloping what already existed instead of rewriting it: a single HTML/CSS/JS file with an animated Second Brain graph and native browser voice, then a Node-only "antenna" server (zero dependencies) giving the app access to my agenda, email and news without breaking CORS, and finally a second, fully local engine via Ollama running alongside Claude in the cloud.
keyDecisions: Agenda: instead of integrating Google Calendar (as the original plan called for), Jarvis reuses my existing agenda-pessoal app's API — this removed an entire ICS parser from scope, a real simplification, not just reuse.
Every voice-triggered create, edit or delete repeats the action out loud and only executes after explicit confirmation — the same rule the agenda-pessoal Telegram bot already follows.
The local server ("antenna") listens only on 127.0.0.1, with a mandatory allowlist of external domains; anything outside the list gets a 403.
Email is read via IMAP with BODY.PEEK — Jarvis never marks a message as read unless I actually read it.
Dual engine: cloud Claude models or local Ollama (qwen2.5/qwen3) selectable on the fly, with a fully offline template fallback when there's no API key or internet.
result: A working local system: voice and text chat, a Second Brain with 22 notes across 7 areas, agenda read/write with confirmation, email triage into 3 buckets, a news radar, a spoken morning briefing, and a sync button that exports new notes to my Obsidian second brain — never writing directly into the curated pages.
learned: Reusing a system I had already built (agenda-pessoal) instead of integrating an external service cut real complexity, not just code. And a voice assistant needs an offline fallback in every module — if the AI or the network goes down, the app says so clearly and keeps working, never goes silent.
